source: Transcribed from user message. Clarification text normalized for spelling; decision supplement records interpretations separately.

answers.question: Should this interview workflow be separate from applicant testimony given during a council session?
answers.context: Both link to the case/proceeding, but a case-owner interview is not automatically a council hearing or agenda item.
answers.clarification: This is different from applicant testimony; applicant testimony in person is rare.

answers.question: Should only the assigned council member conduct and author these case-investigation interviews?
answers.context: Use Other to name additional permitted interviewers. Prototype selection of any council member is not yet an approved permission.

answers.question: May admin or secretary enter or upload an interview record on the assigned member’s behalf?
answers.context: Preserve the actual interviewer separately from the person entering the data. This does not authorize applicant appeal supplements on their behalf.

answers.question: Should the interviewee list include either applicant, their priest or Father of Confession, and adult witnesses?
answers.context: These types appear in the prototype. No child interviews or child accounts are proposed.

answers.question: Should a witness or priest be recorded as a case-linked contact without creating a login account?
answers.context: Store only the identity/contact details needed for the interview and preserve their relationship to the case.

answers.question: Should both applicants always be interviewed separately?
answers.context: Use Other if the assigned member may sometimes conduct a joint interview; existing council testimony still never places both applicants together.

answers.question: Should admin or secretary create and version the interview templates?
answers.context: Each interview retains the exact template version used; publishing changes must not rewrite completed interviews.
answers.clarification: They can create their own version, but standardized templates are wanted.

answers.question: Should templates vary by interviewee type, such as applicant, spouse, priest or witness?
answers.context: Use Other to prefer one common template or describe a simpler structure.

answers.question: Should interview templates support English and Arabic versions of the same questions?
answers.context: Keep original answers in the language spoken/entered rather than replacing them with translations.

answers.question: Should the assigned member be able to add case-specific follow-up questions within an interview?
answers.context: Keep the published template unchanged and record which questions were added for this case.

answers.question: Should the template allow both structured fields and rich-text answers?
answers.context: For example dates or Yes/No plus detailed narrative. Use Other to prefer narrative-only interview notes.

answers.question: Should an interview show the selected applicant’s submitted answers beside the template for reference?
answers.context: The interviewer may compare assertions but must not overwrite them through the interview record. Other party information remains separately attributed.
answers.clarification: The template is like a guided questionnaire.

answers.question: Should the interview preserve the prototype metadata: person, actual interviewer, method, date/time, location and duration?
answers.context: Methods currently shown are in person, phone and virtual. Other may refine the list or fields.

answers.question: Should the assigned member be able to save an unfinished interview and resume later?
answers.context: This is an investigation-record draft, separate from the no-draft Send action for a council-hearing update.

answers.question: Should each completed interview be an individual entry in a chronological case-interview log?
answers.context: Allow multiple interviews of the same person without overwriting earlier interviews.

answers.question: Should evidence discussed during an interview be linked to specific questions or notes?
answers.context: Reuse retained file versions. Do not duplicate source files or make the interviewee the owner of someone else’s evidence.

answers.question: Should the assigned member have a separate internal observations/recommendations area alongside the interviewee’s answers?
answers.context: Do not blend council conclusions into the interviewee’s recorded statements.

answers.question: Should recording be optional for ordinary case-owner interviews?
answers.context: Recording capability is requested, but mandatory versus optional is undecided. Council-session applicant testimony remains mandatory audio recording.

answers.question: Should the interviewer record that the interviewee was informed about recording before audio capture starts?
answers.context: This asks for a workflow record; exact institutional wording/policy remains to be supplied, not invented here.

answers.question: Should an interview support both microphone recording in CTM and uploading an existing audio file?
answers.context: Open-source recorder requirement is already noted. Original bytes and the actual recorder/uploader remain recorded.
answers.clarification: Can also record directly from mobile; for now it is a web app.

answers.question: Should interview recording support pause/resume and recovery of captured portions after an interruption?
answers.context: Recovery must preserve the actual timeline and gaps, without inventing missing audio.

answers.question: Should the no-fixed-duration/file-size-cap rule for council testimony also apply to these investigation interview recordings?
answers.context: This extends the testimony exception to interview recordings. Ordinary applicant audio attachments would retain their existing limit.

answers.question: Should the interviewer be able to mark the current template question while recording so transcript segments can link to it?
answers.context: Markers guide navigation; they do not establish that every spoken statement is an answer to that question.
answers.clarification: Optional; each template has a number.

answers.question: Should saving an interview recording automatically queue transcription through the approved-for-interviews AI API?
answers.context: Testimony AI processing is already requested; this question explicitly extends external audio processing to case-owner interviews. Provider selection comes later.

answers.question: Should interview transcripts use the same language behavior as testimony: original transcript, English/Arabic translation, and all three versions for mixed speech?
answers.context: Include timestamps and speaker labels; preserve the source recording and original AI output.

answers.question: Should AI suggest which transcript passages answer each template question, for the assigned member to review?
answers.context: Suggestions never become verified interview answers automatically and must link back to timestamped source audio.

answers.question: Should the assigned member review and correct generated interview text before other council members can read it?
answers.context: Use Other if admin/secretary should review instead or also. Every correction retains author/time and earlier versions.

answers.question: Should manually typed interview answers remain separate from the AI transcript even after review?
answers.context: This avoids presenting edited summaries as verbatim testimony; both can reference the original audio.

answers.question: Should unfinished interview records be visible only to the assigned member, admin and secretary?
answers.context: Use Other if all council should see them immediately or if drafts should be author-only. Applicant drafts remain governed separately.

answers.question: Should completed interviews, audio and reviewed transcripts be visible to all authorized council members?
answers.context: No applicant access is inferred. Use Other to specify a narrower audience.

answers.question: Should interview records, recordings and transcripts remain council-only, with any applicant-facing request sent through normal case messages?
answers.context: This keeps internal investigation material separate from the applicant’s own form history.

answers.question: Should the original interviewer be the only person able to revise their completed interview narrative while the case is open?
answers.context: Use Other to allow admin/secretary corrections or the newly assigned member. Preserve every version; closure freezes substantive source records.

answers.question: After reassignment, should the new assigned member add follow-up interviews rather than rewrite the earlier interviewer’s narrative?
answers.context: Earlier authorship and recordings remain intact; they may be read under the approved council scope.

answers.question: Should the assigned member choose reviewed interview findings for the case-hearing briefing instead of automatically sharing the entire transcript?
answers.context: Council source material remains accessible under its permission rules. No automatic decree content or applicant disclosure is implied.
